question: Which small changes around P0554 most affect galaxy rotation, derived cluster lensing, raw cluster image positions, root topology, and Solar-System bounds when all ordinary lens geometries and the universal amplitude are held fixed?

evaluation.universal_q_rule: Keep q fixed at the P0554 value except in the explicit q low/high pair; do not refit any formula parameter.
evaluation.galaxy: Use all 131 SPARC galaxies and the untouched outer-radius split with the previously fixed nuisance parameters.
evaluation.derived_cluster: Use all 84 CLASH equivalent-acceleration points in 20 systems with no cluster refit; this is a conventional-GR-derived target.
evaluation.raw_RXJ2129: Profile training-family source positions at the frozen P0554 geometry and solve seven held-out image roots; no geometry or gravity refit.
evaluation.raw_four_cluster: Profile training-family source positions at each frozen P0554 scalar geometry and solve eleven held-out roots across MACS0329, MACS0429, MACS1115, and MACS1931; no geometry or gravity refit.
evaluation.solar: Evaluate the same Cassini, Earth, Saturn, and Mercury proxy equations used in the P0554 parent search.

impact_rules.pairwise_RMS_rule: Compare low and high only on systems where both variants have every held-out root; never call a dropped root an RMS improvement.

claim_limits: This is a local sensitivity experiment around a post-hoc P0554 law, not a fresh theory-selection sample.
CLASH equivalent accelerations are derived from conventional NFW lens profiles and are not raw theory-neutral lensing observables.
The five raw cluster systems and their geometries are spent at project level; holding geometry fixed isolates formula response but is not a full predictive refit.
The Solar tests are analytic weak-field proxies rather than an ephemeris likelihood.
A large local effect identifies a consequential parameter; it does not imply that either direction is physically correct.
